sys_atf_test.name: Day-2 SAM: push telemetry excludes synthetic rows from monitoring counts and correlationReport joins lineage to evidence
sys_atf_test.description: recordPushOutcome writes a stamped row per attempt; dailyOutcomeCounts/sustainedFailureCheck must exclude synthetic (test_mode) rows and must count non-synthetic ones; correlationReport joins a SAM request id across the lineage row and the evidence table.

sys_atf_step.description: Precondition, plus recordPushOutcome's own contract: it writes a real row (this method has no test_mode short-circuit — see its header) stamped record_type=sam_push_outcome and synthetic=true, since this whole run is under test_mode.

Monitoring must exclude synthetic rows: write three more refused outcomes under test_mode (synthetic=true), then assert dailyOutcomeCounts and sustainedFailureCheck report the SAME numbers as before writing them — a sub-prod ATF run must never move a production dashboard.

Monitoring DOES count real (non-synthetic) rows: insert one push-outcome row directly with synthetic=false (simulating a production write, since recordPushOutcome itself always stamps synthetic=true while test_mode is on for this run) and assert the counts move by exactly one.
correlationReport joins a SAM request id across the lineage row and the evidence table -- the dashboard/report Tier-2 item 6 asks for.

REGRESSION: a reason code containing whitespace must bucket under its own full value. The previous implementation packed the code into business_need and recovered it with a non-whitespace capture, which truncates at the first space — and Day2Env.scrub replaces carriage return, newline and tab WITH A SPACE, so scrubbing could itself introduce the separator that split the code. Grouping on the reason_code column removes the failure mode rather than escaping around it.
